explanation.title: Spanish Reported Speech: Relaying What Others Say

sections.subtitle: Reporting Statements: Present Reporting
sections.content: REPORTED SPEECH (indirect speech) relays what someone said without quoting exactly. Use DICE QUE (says that) or DIJO QUE (said that) to introduce reported statements. PRESENT REPORTING: When reporting verb is in present (dice que), tenses often stay the same. DIRECT: 'Tengo hambre' (I'm hungry). REPORTED: 'Dice que tiene hambre' (He says he's hungry - present stays present). DIRECT: 'Voy al cine' (I'm going to the cinema). REPORTED: 'Dice que va al cine' (She says she's going to the cinema). DIRECT: 'He comido' (I've eaten). REPORTED: 'Dice que ha comido' (He says he's eaten - present perfect stays). Subject pronouns often change: yo → él/ella, nosotros → ellos. Pattern: DICE QUE + usually same tenses as original. Examples: 'María dice: "Estoy cansada"' → 'María dice que está cansada' (María says she's tired). 'Juan dice: "Quiero café"' → 'Juan dice que quiere café' (Juan says he wants coffee). Note that QUE is required in Spanish (unlike English where 'that' is often optional).

sections.subtitle: Reporting Statements: Past Reporting & Tense Changes
sections.content: PAST REPORTING: When reporting verb is in past (dijo que), tenses shift backward. PRESENT → IMPERFECT: DIRECT: 'Tengo hambre' (I'm hungry - present). REPORTED: 'Dijo que tenía hambre' (He said he was hungry - imperfect). DIRECT: 'Estoy cansada' (I'm tired). REPORTED: 'Dijo que estaba cansada' (She said she was tired). PRETERITE/IMPERFECT → stay or shift to PLUPERFECT: DIRECT: 'Comí pizza' (I ate pizza - preterite). REPORTED: 'Dijo que había comido pizza' or 'Dijo que comió pizza' (Said he had eaten/ate pizza). PRESENT PERFECT → PLUPERFECT: DIRECT: 'He terminado' (I've finished). REPORTED: 'Dijo que había terminado' (Said he had finished). FUTURE → CONDITIONAL: DIRECT: 'Vendré mañana' (I'll come tomorrow - future). REPORTED: 'Dijo que vendría mañana' (He said he would come tomorrow - conditional). CONDITIONAL → stays CONDITIONAL: 'Dijo que iría' → 'Dijo que dijo que iría'. Pattern: DIJO QUE + backshift tenses one step into past.

sections.subtitle: Reporting Questions
sections.content: REPORTED QUESTIONS transform direct questions into indirect statements. Remove question marks and adjust word order. YES/NO QUESTIONS: Use SI (if/whether) to introduce. DIRECT: '¿Tienes hambre?' (Are you hungry?). REPORTED: 'Pregunta si tienes hambre' (He asks if/whether you're hungry). 'Me preguntó si tenía hambre' (He asked me if I was hungry - past, so tenía shifts to imperfect). WH-QUESTIONS: Keep the question word but remove question marks. DIRECT: '¿Dónde vives?' (Where do you live?). REPORTED: 'Pregunta dónde vivo' (He asks where I live). '¿Qué quieres?' (What do you want?). REPORTED: 'Me preguntó qué quería' (He asked me what I wanted - past reporting, so quería shifts to imperfect). DIRECT: '¿Cuándo vendrás?' (When will you come?). REPORTED: 'Preguntó cuándo vendría' (He asked when I would come - future → conditional in past reporting). Pattern: Pregunta/Preguntó + SI (yes/no) or QUESTION WORD + adjusted statement. Word order becomes statement order (not inverted). No question marks in reported questions.

sections.subtitle: Reporting Commands & Requests
sections.content: REPORTED COMMANDS use specific verbs + QUE + SUBJUNCTIVE (always!). Common reporting verbs: DECIR (tell), PEDIR (ask/request), MANDAR (order), ROGAR (beg), ACONSEJAR (advise), ORDENAR (command), SUGERIR (suggest). DIRECT COMMAND: 'Come la sopa' (Eat the soup - tú command). REPORTED: 'Me dice que coma la sopa' (He tells me to eat the soup - present subjunctive). 'Me dijo que comiera la sopa' (He told me to eat the soup - imperfect subjunctive with past reporting). NEGATIVE COMMAND: 'No hables' (Don't talk). REPORTED: 'Me pide que no hable' (He asks me not to talk - subjunctive). Pattern: Present reporting + present subjunctive. Past reporting + imperfect subjunctive. More examples: DIRECT: 'Estudia más' (Study more). REPORTED: 'Mi madre me dice que estudie más' (My mother tells me to study more). DIRECT: 'Ven aquí' (Come here). REPORTED: 'Me dijo que viniera aquí' (He told me to come here - past, so imperfect subjunctive). REQUESTS: 'Me pidió que le ayudara' (He asked me to help him). Always use subjunctive after these reporting verbs when reporting commands/requests.

sections.subtitle: Time & Place Expression Changes
sections.content: When reporting speech, time and place words shift perspective. TIME CHANGES (especially with past reporting): HOY (today) → ESE DÍA/AQUEL DÍA (that day). 'Hoy estoy ocupado' → 'Dijo que ese día estaba ocupado' (Said that day he was busy). MAÑANA (tomorrow) → AL DÍA SIGUIENTE (the next day). 'Vendré mañana' → 'Dijo que vendría al día siguiente' (Said he would come the next day). AYER (yesterday) → EL DÍA ANTERIOR (the day before). 'Ayer fui al cine' → 'Dijo que el día anterior había ido al cine' (Said the day before he had gone). AHORA (now) → ENTONCES (then). 'Ahora no puedo' → 'Dijo que entonces no podía' (Said then he couldn't). ESTA SEMANA (this week) → ESA SEMANA (that week). PLACE CHANGES: AQUÍ/ACÁ (here) → ALLÍ/ALLÁ (there). 'Estoy aquí' → 'Dijo que estaba allí' (Said he was there). ESTE/ESTA (this) → ESE/ESA or AQUEL/AQUELLA (that). 'Este libro es bueno' → 'Dijo que ese libro era bueno' (Said that book was good). The shift reflects speaker's new perspective and time distance from original statement.

sections.subtitle: Sequence of Tenses & Complex Reporting
sections.content: SEQUENCE OF TENSES: Maintain logical time relationships when backshifting. When main verb is past, subordinate clauses shift accordingly. 'Sé que María está enferma' (I know María is sick - present knows present). → 'Sabía que María estaba enferma' (I knew María was sick - past knew imperfect). 'Creo que vendrá' (I think he'll come - present thinks future). → 'Creí que vendría' (I thought he would come - past thought conditional). MULTIPLE LEVELS: 'Juan dice: "María dijo que vendría"' (Juan says: 'María said she would come'). → 'Juan dice que María dijo que vendría' (Juan says that María said she would come). SUBJUNCTIVE in reported speech: If original uses subjunctive, it typically stays subjunctive. 'Quiero que vengas' (I want you to come). → 'Dijo que quería que viniera' (He said he wanted me to come - both shift but remain subjunctive). MIXING STATEMENTS: 'Me dijo que estaba cansado y que se iría pronto' (He told me he was tired and that he would leave soon - coordinating reported clauses). Use QUE before each clause for clarity. The key is maintaining temporal and logical consistency throughout the reported sequence.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Tengo hambre'. REPORTED: 'Dice que ___'

answers.text: tiene hambre (present stays with present reporting)

questions.hint: Present reporting (dice que) usually keeps same tenses. Present → present.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Estoy cansado'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'

answers.text: estaba cansado (present → imperfect with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting (dijo que) backshifts tenses. Present → imperfect.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Vendré mañana'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'

answers.text: vendría mañana (future → conditional with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting (dijo que) backshifts. Future → conditional (would come).

questions.question: DIRECT: 'He terminado'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'
questions.hint: Past reporting backshifts. Present perfect → pluperfect (had finished).

questions.question: 'María dice: "Quiero café"'. How to report?
questions.hint: Present reporting keeps tenses. QUE is required: dice QUE quiere.

questions.question: Is QUE required in Spanish reported speech?

answers.text: Yes (dice que, dijo que - que is required)

questions.hint: QUE is required in Spanish: dice QUE, dijo QUE (unlike English where 'that' is optional).

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Tienes hambre?'. How to report in present?
questions.hint: Yes/No questions use SI (if/whether): Pregunta SI tengo hambre.

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Dónde vives?'. How to report in present?
questions.hint: Wh-questions keep question word, remove question marks: Pregunta DÓNDE vivo (statement order).

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Cuándo vendrás?'. REPORTED: 'Me preguntó cuándo ___'
questions.hint: Past reporting question: future → conditional. Asked when I WOULD come.

questions.question: Do reported questions use question marks?

answers.text: No (they become statements: Pregunta dónde vivo)

questions.hint: Reported questions become statements, no question marks: Pregunta dónde vivo (not ¿dónde vivo?).

questions.question: DIRECT COMMAND: 'Come la sopa'. REPORTED: 'Me dice que ___'
questions.hint: Reported commands use subjunctive. Present reporting → present subjunctive: que coma.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Estudia más'. REPORTED: 'Mi madre me dijo que ___'

answers.text: estudiara más (imperfect subjunctive with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting of commands → imperfect subjunctive: dijo que estudiara.

questions.question: What mood is used for reported commands?
questions.hint: Reported commands ALWAYS use subjunctive: dice que coma, dijo que comiera.

questions.question: 'Me pidió que le ayudara' - What was the original request?
questions.hint: Pidió que + imperfect subjunctive = reported past request. He asked me to help him.

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Hoy estoy ocupado'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ estaba ocupado'
questions.hint: Time shift with past reporting: HOY (today) → ESE DÍA (that day).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Vendré mañana'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que vendría ___'
questions.hint: Time shift: MAÑANA (tomorrow) → AL DÍA SIGUIENTE (the next day).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Ayer fui al cine'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ había ido al cine'
questions.hint: Time shift: AYER (yesterday) → EL DÍA ANTERIOR (the day before).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Ahora no puedo'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ no podía'
questions.hint: Time shift: AHORA (now) → ENTONCES (then).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Estoy aquí'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que estaba ___'
questions.hint: Place shift: AQUÍ (here) → ALLÍ (there) - perspective changes to reporter's location.

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Este libro es bueno'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ libro era bueno'
questions.hint: Demonstrative shift: ESTE (this) → ESE/AQUEL (that).

questions.question: 'Sé que María está enferma' → 'Sabía que María ___'
questions.hint: Sequence of tenses: main verb past, subordinate shifts accordingly. Knew (past) → was sick (imperfect).

questions.question: 'Creo que vendrá' → 'Creí que ___'
questions.hint: Sequence: main verb past, future shifts to conditional. Thought (past) → would come (conditional).

questions.question: 'Quiero que vengas' → 'Dijo que quería que ___'
questions.hint: Subjunctive in reported speech stays subjunctive but backshifts: vengas → viniera.

questions.question: 'Me dijo que estaba cansado y que ___ pronto' (se iría / se irá)

answers.text: se iría (conditional - maintains past reporting consistency)

questions.hint: Maintain consistency in reported sequence. Both clauses with past reporting use backshifted tenses: estaba (imperfect), se iría (conditional).
